experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski schools for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure
experiences.description: Embark on a guided family snowshoeing tour across the Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps. A certified guide leads the group through stunning frozen landscapes, teaching kids about glacial formations and alpine ecology. Gear is included in the tour price and the pace is family-friendly.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Preda-Bergün Run
experiences.description: Experience one of the most famous natural toboggan runs in Switzerland, stretching 6km from Preda down to Bergün. The run is illuminated at night for evening rides, making it magical for families. Sleds are rented locally and the train ride back up is part of the fun, offering breathtaking valley views.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Visit a traditional alpine dairy farm in Gruyères to watch artisan cheese-making, then sit down for an authentic Swiss fondue dinner with locally produced Gruyère and Emmental cheese. This hands-on cultural experience gives families a deep taste of Swiss mountain heritage and cuisine, with kid-friendly portions available.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, known as the Top of Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, visit the Sphinx Observatory, and let kids play in the snow at the highest railway station in Europe. The panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier are unforgettable and the experience is accessible to all ages.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00 on flight LH. Take the SBB Swiss train from Zurich Airport to Grindelwald via Interlaken Ost (approximately 2.5–3 hours, book in advance for best budget fares using a Swiss Travel Pass or saver ticket). Check in to Grindelwald Boutique Stay in the Jungfrau Region. Drop off luggage and take a short orientation stroll through Grindelwald village to get your bearings, spot the iconic Eiger North Face backdrop, and locate the ski rental shops for tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Grindelwald's main street (Dorfstrasse) on foot. Browse local shops and pick up snacks or groceries at the Coop or Migros supermarket in the village center to stock up on budget breakfast and snack supplies for the week. Enjoy a relaxed first evening settling into the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before landing — budget CHF 10–15.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich or buy from a kiosk at Zurich Airport or on the train — budget CHF 8–12.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Coop or Migros in Grindelwald (pasta, soup, bread and cheese) — budget CHF 10–15 per person. Alternatively, try a takeaway Bratwurst or Rösti from a local village snack stand for CHF 12–18.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass (if not already done) or a regional Jungfrau Travel Pass for discounted train and cable car fares throughout the week. Book ski rentals in advance online (e.g., Intersport Grindelwald) for better rates. Pick up a free Grindelwald tourist map from the hotel or tourist office.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the accommodation using groceries purchased the night before. Head to Grindelwald First ski area — take the First Gondola from the village center (Jungfrau Travel Pass holders ride at a discount). Spend the morning skiing or snowboarding on the beginner-to-intermediate slopes of First (2,168m). Families with children can take ski lessons through the Grindelwald Ski School (book in advance for group lesson discounts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First ski area slopes. Take a break and enjoy the panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau from the First Cliff Walk — a free-to-walk suspension walkway offering dramatic mountain views. Families can also try the First Flyer zip line or First Glider (additional cost ~CHF 25–35 per person) as a thrilling non-ski activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by gondola. Warm up with a hot chocolate or Glühwein at one of the village cafés. Prepare dinner at the accommodation or visit a local budget-friendly restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — muesli, bread, cheese, yogurt from Coop/Migros — CHF 3–5 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and thermos drinks to eat on the mountain, or grab a simple meal at the First mountain restaurant (soup and bread ~CHF 15–20). Avoid full sit-down mountain restaurant meals to save budget.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — a local favorite offering affordable Swiss fondue and raclette in a cozy chalet setting — CHF 20–30 per person. Alternatively, self-cater pasta with cheese sauce — CHF 5–8 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ski rental from Intersport or Grindelwald Sports typically costs CHF 35–50/day for adults and CHF 20–30/day for children when booked online in advance. A day ski pass for First area costs approximately CHF 65–75 for adults; look for family passes or multi-day passes for savings. Dress in warm, waterproof layers — temperatures at altitude can drop to -10°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation. Take the Grindelwald–Wengen–Kleine Scheidegg train (scenic cogwheel railway, covered by Jungfrau Travel Pass discount) up to Kleine Scheidegg (2,061m). Begin skiing the Kleine Scheidegg–Männlichen ski area, which connects to a vast network of runs suitable for all levels. The wide open pistes here are ideal for families and intermediate skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing the Kleine Scheidegg area. Take the Lauberhorn run — one of the most famous downhill ski routes in the world (used in World Cup racing). Families with younger children can enjoy gentler blue runs near Wengen. If the weather is clear, take a short break to admire the stunning Jungfrau Railway station and the towering Eiger face up close.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by cogwheel train. Visit the Grindelwald Ice Rink (Sportzentrum Grindelwald) for a fun family evening of ice skating — entry and skate hire approximately CHF 10–15 per person, making it a very budget-friendly activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — eggs, toast, fruit — CHF 3–5 per person.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the mountain (sandwiches, energy bars, thermos of hot soup). Alternatively, try the self-service restaurant at Kleine Scheidegg station for a budget plate of the day (~CHF 18–22).
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty Swiss-style dinner at accommodation — Rösti with fried eggs and cheese (a classic Swiss budget meal) using groceries — CHF 6–10 per person. Or try Pizzeria da Salvi in Grindelwald for affordable pizza and pasta — CHF 18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The cogwheel train between Grindelwald and Kleine Scheidegg is scenic and highly recommended even without skiing. Multi-day ski passes covering both First and Kleine Scheidegg–Männlichen areas offer better value — check the Jungfrau Ski Region website for current pricing and family discounts. Keep children close on the Kleine Scheidegg pistes as some runs merge with faster intermediate and advanced skiers.

day_by_day.morning: Self-catered breakfast. Take a rest day from skiing to explore the broader Jungfrau Region on a budget. Board the Jungfrau Railway from Grindelwald Grund station toward Jungfraujoch — 'Top of Europe' (3,454m). Note: a full Jungfraujoch ticket is expensive (~CHF 145–175 per adult), but the Jungfrau Travel Pass offers significant discounts. Alternatively, ride only to Eigergletscher station (~CHF 40–60 with pass discount) for stunning glacier and Eiger views without the full summit price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Alight at Eigergletscher (2,320m) and enjoy a free walk along the marked snow trail with breathtaking views of the Aletsch Glacier and surrounding peaks. Take the train back down to Grindelwald and visit the free Grindelwald Museum (small local history museum) to learn about the region's alpine heritage. Alternatively, take a leisurely snowshoe walk on the marked free snowshoe trail around the lower Grindelwald valley floor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald village. Browse the village shops for Swiss souvenirs — look for affordable options like Swiss chocolate bars (CHF 2–4), postcards, and small wooden crafts. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — porridge with dried fruit and nuts, coffee — CHF 3–4 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from accommodation for the train excursion. Eat at Eigergletscher station picnic area or on the train platform with mountain views — CHF 0 (packed).
meals.dinner: Try Restaurant Firestarter in Grindelwald for affordable burgers, wraps, and local dishes — CHF 18–28 per person. Or self-cater a Swiss cheese fondue at the accommodation using a fondue set (available at Coop/Migros for ~CHF 15–20 for the set, CHF 10–15 for cheese and bread for a family) for a memorable and budget-friendly Swiss experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' visit is iconic but costly. Check the Jungfrau Railway website for 'Good Morning Ticket' early-bird discounts (departure before 07:00, savings of ~CHF 20–30 per adult). Families with children under 16 often receive free or heavily discounted tickets with a Swiss Family Card — verify current promotions. Snowshoe rentals available in Grindelwald from ~CHF 15/day if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Self-catered breakfast. Today, explore the Mürren ski area — a car-free alpine village offering excellent skiing and stunning Jungfrau panoramas. Travel from Grindelwald by bus to Lauterbrunnen, then cable car to Grütschalp, then mountain railway to Mürren (approximately 1 hour total, covered by Jungfrau Travel Pass discount). Spend the morning skiing Mürren's varied terrain — excellent for intermediate to advanced skiers, with family-friendly runs available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing in Mürren. Take the Schilthorn cable car up to the Piz Glória revolving restaurant (2,970m) — famous as the James Bond 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service' filming location. Entry to the Piz Glória viewing platform is included with the cable car ticket (~CHF 30–40 with pass discount). Enjoy 360-degree views of 200+ Alpine peaks. Kids love the free James Bond multimedia exhibition inside. Return to Mürren and ski down before taking the return journey to Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the accommodation. Treat the family to a budget-friendly Swiss chocolate tasting session using chocolates purchased from Coop/Migros (Lindt, Toblerone, Frey brands all available at supermarket prices — CHF 2–5 per bar). Play board games or card games as a family evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — bread, jam, Swiss cheese, hot drinks — CHF 3–5 per person.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Piz Glória self-service cafeteria for a budget meal with unbeatable views — soup and a roll ~CHF 12–16. Or pack lunch and eat on the Mürren slopes.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — hearty lentil or vegetable soup with crusty bread and Swiss cheese — CHF 5–8 per person. Or try Stägerstübli restaurant in Grindelwald for traditional Swiss cuisine at moderate prices — CHF 22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The journey to Mürren is part of the adventure — the Lauterbrunnen valley is one of the most scenic in Switzerland with 72 waterfalls. Mürren is car-free and very family-friendly. The Schilthorn/Piz Glória visit is best on a clear day — check the weather forecast the evening before and swap with Day 6 activities if cloudy. Mürren ski passes can be purchased as part of the Jungfrau Ski Region multi-day pass for best value.

day_by_day.morning: Self-catered breakfast. Dedicate today to family-focused winter activities in and around Grindelwald. Start with the Grindelwald First Toboggan Run — one of the longest natural toboggan runs in the Bernese Oberland (approximately 15km from First down to Grindelwald). Rent toboggans in the village (~CHF 10–15/day rental) and take the First Gondola up. The run is free to use (gondola ticket required) and suitable for families with children aged 5+.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the toboggan run, warm up in the village and visit the free Grindelwald tourist information center to pick up any remaining tips. Head to the Grindelwald Sportzentrum for family swimming and wellness — the indoor pool and spa area offers a budget-friendly afternoon of relaxation (~CHF 15–20 per adult, CHF 8–12 per child). This is a great way for tired muscles to recover after days of skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Take a magical winter evening walk through Grindelwald village, enjoying the illuminated chalets and mountain backdrop at dusk. Stop for a budget Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate at a village café or outdoor market stall (~CHF 4–6 per cup). Pack or prepare a special farewell-style dinner at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — Swiss-style bircher muesli with milk and apple, coffee — CHF 3–4 per person.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch at the Coop restaurant in Grindelwald village — daily hot meal specials typically CHF 12–16 per person, great quality and value.
meals.dinner: Self-catered celebratory dinner — raclette-style meal using a simple electric raclette grill (often provided in Swiss holiday accommodations; if not, available to rent). Buy raclette cheese, potatoes, pickles, and charcuterie from Coop/Migros — CHF 12–18 per person for a festive, authentic Swiss experience.

day_by_day.notes: The First Toboggan Run is weather and condition dependent — confirm it is open the evening before at the Grindelwald tourist office website or by calling First Gondola operations. Saturday can be busier on the slopes and in the village as weekend visitors arrive from Swiss cities — plan toboggan and pool activities to avoid peak ski lift queues. The raclette dinner at home is highly recommended as a memorable, authentic, and very budget-friendly Swiss family experience.

day_by_day.morning: Self-catered breakfast — use up remaining groceries from the week (eggs, bread, cheese, fruit). Pack bags and check out of the Grindelwald Boutique Stay (confirm check-out time with accommodation). Take one final short walk to the base of the Eiger for photos and a last look at the stunning alpine scenery before departing. If time allows, visit the Grindelwald village bakery for a fresh croissant or Swiss pastry as a farewell treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Grindelwald by SBB train toward Zurich Airport (via Interlaken Ost, approximately 2.5–3 hours). Book train tickets in advance for best fares. Use travel time to review photos, rest, and reflect on the week's adventures. Arrive at Zurich Airport with sufficient time for check-in and departure formalities (allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich Airport. Pick up last-minute Swiss chocolate or souvenirs at the airport duty-free shops (Lindt chocolate is available at competitive prices in airport shops). Board return flight.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — use remaining groceries, or treat the family to pastries from the Grindelwald village bakery (~CHF 3–5 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack remaining snacks and sandwiches for the train journey, or purchase a simple meal at Interlaken Ost station (~CHF 10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport — budget options include Coop to go, Marché, or McDonald's (~CHF 15–22 per person). Alternatively, eat a proper meal before reaching the airport in Interlaken or Zurich city if time permits.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm train times from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport the evening before using the SBB app or website — trains run regularly but allow extra time on Sundays as some services may be less frequent. Return all ski rental equipment before leaving Grindelwald (most shops open from 08:00). Validate your Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass for the return journey. Keep all receipts for any VAT refund claims at the airport if applicable.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Grindelwald via train (Zurich HB → Interlaken Ost → Grindelwald, approx. 2.5–3 hrs). Settle into the Boutique Stay, unpack, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village. Visit the local ski rental shop to book equipment and lift passes for the week. Pick up a trail map and get familiar with the resort layout. Stop by the Grindelwald Tourist Office for family activity tips.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the hotel or a nearby village restaurant. Enjoy a hearty Swiss meal to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Interlaken train station — try a Migros or Coop self-service café for sandwiches, soup, and Swiss pastries (budget-friendly, ~CHF 12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — cozy mountain restaurant offering Swiss classics like Rösti, Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, and local beer. Mid-range pricing (~CHF 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ski equipment rental in advance online (e.g., Intersport Grindelwald) to save 10–15%. Purchase a Jungfrau Ski Region multi-day pass at the tourist office or online. Confirm Jungfraujoch excursion reservation if not already done — tickets sell out fast in February.

day_by_day.morning: First day on the slopes! Head to Grindelwald First ski area (gondola departs from the village center). Warm up on the wide, groomed blue and red runs of the First ski zone. Ideal for families and intermediate skiers. Stunning views of the Eiger north face.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing — explore the Oberjoch and Schreckfeld sectors. Take a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at Bergrestaurant First (2,168m). More adventurous family members can try the First Flyer zip line or First Glider as an add-on activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to village by gondola. Relax at the hotel, then head out for a family-friendly dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — typically included or available for ~CHF 18–22; enjoy muesli, fresh bread, cold cuts, and Swiss cheese
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant First on the mountain — self-service cafeteria style. Try the Älplermagronen (Swiss alpine mac & cheese with applesauce) or daily soup (~CHF 18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Memory in Grindelwald — popular mid-range spot with Swiss and international dishes, great for families. Try the cheese fondue as a group (~CHF 28–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rent helmets for all children — mandatory for under-14s on many Swiss slopes. Start early (lifts open ~8:30am) to avoid midday crowds. Apply high-SPF sunscreen even on cloudy days — UV rays are intense at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion — depart Grindelwald by 8:00am on the cogwheel train via Kleine Scheidegg to Jungfraujoch (3,454m). Allow 2.5 hours for the ascent. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory viewing deck, and the eternal snow plateau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — try the Snow Fun Park (sledding, snow tubing, and ski activities on the plateau, included in some packages). Descend back to Kleine Scheidegg by early afternoon and enjoy a few runs on the Kleine Scheidegg–Wengen ski area on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by 17:00. Warm up at the hotel spa or pool if available. Casual dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before 7:30am departure
meals.lunch: Self-Service Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — reasonably priced for the altitude. Try the hot soup, pasta, or Swiss daily special (~CHF 22–30 per person). Tip: bring snacks as prices are elevated at the top
meals.dinner: Pizzeria da Salvi, Grindelwald — relaxed, family-friendly Italian-Swiss restaurant. Pizzas, pasta, and salads (~CHF 22–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance — February is peak season. Consider the 'Good Morning Ticket' (depart before 9am) for a significant discount (~CHF 145 vs. CHF 175 standard adult). Dress in very warm layers — temperatures at the top can be -15°C or lower. Children under 16 receive discounted tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — join a guided family snowshoeing tour departing from Grindelwald. The tour explores the lower Aletsch Glacier approach and surrounding alpine terrain. Guides provide all equipment and safety briefing. Suitable for children aged 6+.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the snowshoeing tour (typically ends around 13:00–14:00), enjoy a relaxed afternoon back in the village. Visit the Grindelwald Museum for a short cultural stop, or browse local shops for Swiss chocolate, watches, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Family-friendly fondue evening — book a traditional fondue experience at a local chalet restaurant for a memorable group dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by many snowshoeing tour operators, or stop at Café 3692 in Grindelwald post-tour for homemade soups and sandwiches (~CHF 15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Chalet Restaurant Gydisdorf — authentic Swiss chalet setting with cheese fondue, raclette, and local wine. Perfect family atmosphere (~CHF 35–50 per person including fondue set)

day_by_day.notes: Book the glacier snowshoeing tour through Grindelwald Sports or Outdoor Interlaken — tours typically run 4–5 hours and cost CHF 55–75 per adult, CHF 35–45 per child. Waterproof pants and warm gloves are essential. This is a lighter activity day — ideal mid-week recovery from skiing.

day_by_day.morning: Full ski day on the Männlichen–Kleine Scheidegg ski area. Take the Grindelwald–Männlichen gondola (one of the world's longest at 6.2km) to the top. Enjoy panoramic Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views. Ski the Royal Walk ridge or tackle the long red runs back toward Kleine Scheidegg.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing the Wengen side of the mountain — accessible via Kleine Scheidegg. Wengen runs are long, scenic, and family-friendly. Take the cogwheel train back to Grindelwald in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at Bar 3000 or Espresso Bar in Grindelwald village. Then a relaxed dinner to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Restaurant Grindelwaldblick at Kleine Scheidegg — sit-down mountain restaurant with table service. Try the Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) starter and a hearty Wurst with Rösti (~CHF 25–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Hotel Spinne Restaurant, Grindelwald — well-regarded mid-range hotel restaurant with Swiss and European cuisine. Great for families (~CHF 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Friday tends to be busier on slopes as weekend visitors arrive — head to lifts early (by 8:30am). The Männlichen gondola can have queues after 9:30am in peak season. The Wengen–Lauberhorn area is historically significant — site of the famous Lauberhorn downhill race.

day_by_day.morning: Tobogganing on the Preda-Bergün Run — depart Grindelwald by train to Bergün (approx. 1.5 hrs via Interlaken and Chur direction). This is a day trip to experience one of Switzerland's most famous 6km natural toboggan runs. Sleds available to rent on-site. Multiple runs possible in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue tobogganing or explore Bergün village — a charming Romansh-speaking village with a historic center. Return to Grindelwald by mid-to-late afternoon (allow 2 hrs travel back).
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Grindelwald — celebrate the trip with a special dinner at one of the village's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before train departure
meals.lunch: Restaurant Kurhaus Bergün near the toboggan run — traditional Swiss mountain food, warming soups, hot chocolate, and Rösti (~CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter, Grindelwald — lively, modern Swiss restaurant with wood-fired dishes, craft beers, and a great atmosphere for families (~CHF 32–48 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Preda-Bergün toboggan run is open evenings with lighting on select nights — check the schedule at bergun.ch. Sled rental costs ~CHF 12 per day. The run is suitable for children aged 5+ with adult supervision. Train pass (Swiss Travel Pass or day ticket) covers the journey. Book return trains in advance on weekends as they fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — join a morning tour to a traditional alpine dairy farm in the Gruyères region (reachable by train, ~1.5 hrs). Watch artisan cheese-making demonstrations, learn about the history of Swiss cheese, and sample fresh Gruyère and other local varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the included fondue lunch at the farm, then explore the medieval Château de Gruyères (castle) — a fascinating family-friendly cultural stop with beautiful views. Return to Grindelwald by late afternoon for final packing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner back in Grindelwald. Reflect on the week's adventures over a final Swiss meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience at the Gruyères dairy farm — traditional fondue, bread, charcuterie, and local wine or juice (~CHF 45–60 per person including experience fee)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Alte Post, Grindelwald — historic village inn with classic Swiss dishes. Try the Entrecôte with herb butter or the Züri-Gschnätzlets for a proper Swiss farewell (~CHF 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Gruyères cheese experience through La Maison du Gruyère (lamaisondugruyere.ch) — tours run at set times and advance booking is recommended. If departure flight is on Feb 22, allow ample time for the train journey (Grindelwald → Interlaken → Bern/Zurich, ~2.5–3 hrs). Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate and cheese as gifts at Gruyères before returning.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, known as the Top of Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, visit the Sphinx Observatory, and let kids play in the snow at the highest railway station in Europe. The panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier are unforgettable and the experience is accessible to all ages.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Allow time for baggage collection, customs, and private transfer from Zurich Airport to Grindelwald (approx. 2.5–3 hours via luxury chauffeured car or scenic train via Interlaken).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Grindelwald Boutique Stay in the Jungfrau Region. Check in, settle into your luxury suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a relaxed stroll through Grindelwald village to orientate yourselves — admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face and pick up any ski passes or equipment rentals at a premium ski shop in the village.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private welcome dinner at the hotel's gourmet restaurant or a nearby fine dining establishment. Unwind and prepare for the exciting week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge.
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Zurich Airport business/first class lounge during transit.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Restaurant Memories (Grand Hotel Regina, Grindelwald) — celebrated for its contemporary Alpine cuisine with panoramic Eiger views. Tasting menu with Swiss wine pairing recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer from Zurich Airport to Grindelwald. Confirm ski rental and lift pass bookings upon arrival. Bring warm layers as Grindelwald sits at approx. 1,034m elevation and February temperatures can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Begin your alpine ski adventure on the world-class Grindelwald First ski area. Book a private family ski instructor for a half-day morning session covering technique and safety on groomed blue and red runs. The First area offers stunning views of the Wetterhorn and is ideal for mixed-ability family groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing across the interconnected Kleine Scheidegg slopes, linking Grindelwald to Wengen. Explore the legendary Lauberhorn piste — one of the most famous ski runs in the world. Take a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at one of the mountain-top ski chalets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa session — enjoy the heated indoor pool, sauna, and steam room to soothe tired muscles. Dress for a sophisticated dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the hotel featuring Swiss cheeses, cold cuts, freshly baked breads, bircher muesli, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Grindelwaldblick on the mountain — enjoy raclette, rösti, and hearty Alpine soups with spectacular Eiger views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chalet Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — a cozy, upscale chalet restaurant known for its premium fondue, Angus beef, and Swiss Pinot Noir selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructors in advance through the Swiss Ski School Grindelwald. Ensure all family members have properly fitted helmets and ski gear. Lift passes for the Jungfrau Ski Region cover all interconnected areas.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion — Board the iconic cogwheel train from Grindelwald Grund station. Travel through the dramatic Eiger tunnel to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, walk on the glacier plateau, and marvel at sweeping views across the Aletsch Glacier and into France, Germany, and Italy on clear days. Dress in your warmest layers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — visit the Sphinx Observatory, try the thrilling Snow Fun Park (zip lines, snow tubing, and snow disc rides perfect for families), and browse the Top of Europe visitor center. Begin the descent back to Grindelwald via Kleine Scheidegg in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitif in the hotel lounge with a curated selection of Swiss craft spirits and canapés.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — fuel up well before the high-altitude excursion.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — a self-service mountain restaurant at 3,454m offering hot Alpine dishes, soups, and warm beverages. Alternatively, reserve a table at the upscale Bollywood Restaurant on-site for a unique experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Belvedere Grindelwald's fine dining room — elegant setting with seasonal Swiss cuisine, game dishes, and an extensive wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch excursion is weather-dependent — check the Jungfrau Railway webcam the evening before. Book train tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly in peak February season. Allow at least 30 minutes of acclimatization at the top due to the altitude (3,454m). Children should be briefed on altitude awareness.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — Join a private guided family snowshoeing tour across the Great Aletsch Glacier area, the largest glacier in the Alps (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Your expert mountain guide will lead the family through pristine snow landscapes, pointing out glacial formations, crevasses, and Alpine wildlife tracks. Snowshoes and poles are provided; warm base layers and waterproof outerwear are essential.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tobogganing on the Preda-Bergün Run — After the snowshoeing morning, transfer to the legendary Preda-Bergün natural toboggan run (approx. 1.5 hours by train via Chur — a scenic journey on the Rhaetian Railway). Experience the thrilling 6km natural run descending from Preda to Bergün — a world-famous family highlight. Multiple runs are possible as a shuttle train returns toboggans to the top.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by early evening. Enjoy a family-friendly but luxurious dinner celebrating an action-packed day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with energizing options — porridge, protein-rich eggs, smoked salmon, and fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, Swiss chocolate, thermos of hot soup, and warm beverages to enjoy on the glacier.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Firestorm, Grindelwald — known for premium wood-fired meats, truffle pasta, and a family-welcoming atmosphere with an impressive cocktail and mocktail menu.

day_by_day.notes: The Preda-Bergün toboggan run operates in the evenings under floodlights as well — confirm current operating hours. Toboggan rental is available on-site. The glacier snowshoeing tour requires a minimum fitness level and appropriate layering. Pre-book the private guide through a certified Grindelwald mountain guide agency.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes (Mürren & Schilthorn) — Take the scenic gondola and train combination to the car-free village of Mürren (accessible via Lauterbrunnen). Ski the Schilthorn ski area — immortalized as the James Bond filming location in 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service.' The runs here are more challenging and less crowded, ideal for intermediate to advanced skiers. Families with younger children can enjoy the gentler Mürren village slopes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at the top of the Schilthorn (2,970m) for lunch, then enjoy a private guided off-piste or powder snow experience with a certified ski guide in the Mürren backcountry. Return to Grindelwald by late afternoon via the Lauterbrunnen valley.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a luxury spa evening at the hotel — book a couples' or family wellness package including Alpine herb massages, hot stone treatments, and hydrotherapy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — freshly made waffles, Swiss honey, mountain berry compotes, and Nespresso coffee station.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Piz Gloria Revolving Restaurant, Schilthorn summit — iconic 360-degree panoramic views across 200 Alpine peaks. Enjoy their 'Bond World' themed menu or classic Swiss mountain cuisine.
meals.dinner: In-room premium dining experience — arrange a private chef's tasting menu delivered to your suite, featuring seasonal Swiss delicacies, truffle, and fondue with a curated wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is a car-free village — all transfers are by gondola, cable car, and train. The journey from Grindelwald to Mürren takes approximately 45–60 minutes. Book the Piz Gloria lunch reservation in advance. Check weather and visibility conditions for the Schilthorn summit.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — Depart by private car to Gruyères (approx. 1.5 hours from Grindelwald). Visit the La Maison du Gruyère artisan dairy to witness the traditional cheese-making process with a private guided tour. Explore the beautifully preserved medieval village of Gruyères and visit the Gruyères Castle for a fascinating history lesson the whole family will enjoy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sit down for an authentic, immersive fondue and raclette lunch experience at a traditional Gruyères restaurant. Afterward, visit the HR Giger Museum (unique and memorable for older children and adults) or explore the village boutiques for premium Swiss souvenirs — handmade chocolates, watches, and local cheeses to take home. Return to Grindelwald by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Grindelwald — celebrate the trip with a grand farewell dinner at the finest table available.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with freshly baked croissants, local honey, cold cuts, and barista coffee.
meals.lunch: Fondue and raclette lunch at Restaurant Le Chalet de Gruyères — the quintessential Swiss cultural dining experience with traditional wooden décor, local wines, and artisan cheeses.
meals.dinner: Gala farewell dinner at Restaurant Panorama at a luxury Grindelwald hotel — seven-course tasting menu featuring Alpine ingredients: venison, mountain herbs, glacier water, Swiss truffles, and a Swiss cheese trolley. Paired with a sommelier-curated Swiss and European wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Gruyères is a half-day trip from Grindelwald — arrange a private luxury chauffeur for comfort and flexibility. The La Maison du Gruyère dairy offers private group tours bookable in advance. This day is ideal for a cultural contrast after several high-activity ski days, and is particularly memorable for children.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent hotel breakfast. Take one last scenic walk through Grindelwald village or a gentle snowshoe stroll to a nearby viewpoint for farewell photos of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Visit a premium Swiss watch or chocolate boutique in the village for last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel after a late checkout (pre-arrange with the hotel). Board your private luxury transfer back to Zurich Airport or your onward destination. Enjoy the scenic Swiss landscape one final time on the journey.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — allow ample time at Zurich Airport. Relax in the Zurich Airport SWISS First Class Lounge or Senator Lounge before your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — take your time and savor the final Swiss morning spread with panoramic mountain views.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a Grindelwald café — try a traditional Zopf bread with mountain cheese and a warm Swiss hot chocolate before departure.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Zurich Airport SWISS First Class Lounge or an airside restaurant such as Cervo Restaurant in Terminal E — offering premium Swiss and international cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (12:00–14:00) from the hotel when booking to maximize your final morning. Confirm private transfer timing to ensure you arrive at Zurich Airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Pack your Swiss cheese and chocolates in checked luggage — liquid restrictions apply to fondue sets and wine. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned the evening before or first thing in the morning.
